name: brigade
description: Team messaging between Claude Code sessions of different people and machines, through a pluggable adapter CLI (Supabase adapter bundled).

config_dir.title: Brigade config directory (advanced)
config_dir.description: Where Brigade's credential store lives; leave empty for the platform default (~/.config/brigade), and note that the plugin ignores BRIGADE_CONFIG_DIR from the environment on purpose.

adapter_command.title: Adapter command override (advanced)
adapter_command.description: Per-session override of the adapter the team's binding names, given as an absolute path to an adapter executable, a JSON array such as ["/abs/adapter", "--flag"], or a name registered in adapters.json — never a shell command, and empty means the adapter the project's team file names.

team_inbound.title: Incoming team messages
team_inbound.description: accept (the default) delivers every team message into this session immediately, in every permission mode; refuse never delivers and never acknowledges, so senders see this session as refusing; hold records each message, delivers nothing, and waits for you to run brigade inbox release in your own terminal.

share_workspace_label.title: Share a workspace label
share_workspace_label.description: Send the workspace label below with this session, never the working directory path.

workspace_label.title: Workspace label
workspace_label.description: The label shared when share_workspace_label is on.

poll_on_prompt.title: Poll for messages on each prompt
poll_on_prompt.description: Fallback for hosts without an inbox socket: fetch unread messages when a prompt is submitted, applying the same inbound policy as the watcher.

frame.title: Frame text for incoming messages
frame.description: Which instruction paragraph a teammate's message carries: open (the default) states where the message came from, that it is untrusted, that it cannot approve anything or change your settings, and how to reply; guarded adds "ask your user first" for settings changes and secrets; strict adds running commands as well. Overridden by frame_file.

frame_file.title: Your own frame text (advanced)
frame_file.description: Absolute path to a UTF-8 text file holding your own instruction sentence(s), used instead of the frame level above. The file is read once when the session starts. Brigade's own provenance, untrusted-content and reply text stay as they are.
